## p230 A — Divisions around Hermannstadt and an OKM headquarters move

**Sources on this page:** p230 A3, p230 A4.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-p230-a--divisions-around-hermannstadt-and-an-okm-headquarters-move"></a>


[Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md)

**Record:** surviving third and fourth parts of message A on printed p230;
the source says the first two parts are missing.
**Result:** 462 source coordinates yield 231 baseline-label plaintext
positions. The proposed edition makes eight known-coordinate substitutions.
The further historical `303` division proposal below adds one, bringing
the optional combined edition to **nine** substitutions.
Historical number identifications, separator convention and lexical letter
assignments are separate optional layers; the published key is unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-most-likely-reading"></a>

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-divisions-and-headquarters-movement"></a>

### Divisions and headquarters movement

**Conditional interpretation — readable German with the shared calendar and unit assignments:**

> 226. I. D. nordwestl. Hermannstadt. 16. Ldw. Div. um Muehlbach.
> 218. Div. im Raume Hatszeg, Livazeny. Drittens. Gen. Kdo. 63 Kronstadt.
> 89 und 3L3 Div. um Kronstadt. 7 bayr. Kav. Brig. um Fogaras versammelt.
> OKM verlegt Hauptquart. nach Muehlbach. OKM1ANRZ11U30OP.

**Meaning:** The report gives the positions of withdrawing divisions,
places General Command 63 at Kronstadt, and announces an OKM headquarters
move to Muehlbach. The shared interpretation now identifies the **7th Bavarian
cavalry brigade** around Fogaras. The received division field `3L3` admits
the historically supported **303rd Division** proposal below; the closing
reference remains literal.

The [joint date and unit study](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
assigns `VG=7` from this brigade field and the `217` formation in p229 A1,
with support from Barkóczy-Klopsch's 1923 military history. The November date
in p229 separately fixes `GA=0`. These two assignments bring part 4 from
**113 to 115/115 interpreted positions**, without adding source edits.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-the-303rd-division-one-separately-priced-correction"></a>

#### The 303rd Division: one separately priced correction

Reading the damaged division field as **`303`** gives **89 und 303 Div.
um Kronstadt**. Barkóczy-Klopsch's 1923 order of battle lists the **89th
Infantry Division and 303rd Landsturm Division** together under the
63rd Bavarian corps.
[Printed p11](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/sources/barkoczy_p11.png)
· [Institutional scan](https://real-eod.mtak.hu/8911/1/MTA_AKisAkademiaKonyvtara_043.pdf).
This supports the formation identity without independently proving its
30 November location.

The original middle character is `L`, pair **GG**, at part 4 plaintext
position **7**, from source positions **0 and 86**. Changing source **86
from G to A** gives `GA=0` under the shared date interpretation. The
source glyph is G: this is one added observed-coordinate correction,
not a retranscription. Part 4 then costs **two substitutions** including
the earlier `HEUPT→HAUPT` repair, with no mask fills or frame changes.

The [separate division certificate](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/division_certificate.json)
re-encrypts the proposal under both surviving squares. It also retains
the equally cheap numerical alternatives **313, 373 and 383**; the
external formation list supplies the reason for proposing 303.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-earlier-number-and-letter-interpretations"></a>

#### Earlier number and letter interpretations

The numbers above assume a consistent interpretation of baseline labels:
`X→1`, `J→2`, `8→6`, `4→8`, `5→9`, and `2→3`. Contemporary French intelligence
lists the 226th Infantry, 16th Landwehr, 218th Infantry and 89th Infantry
divisions. The French list itself marks the 89th as `89e D.I.?`; the later
independent Hungarian account lists the 89th without that query. The reading
of General Command 63 is supported by the p163
withdrawal edition under its stated historical and editorial assumptions.
These are conditional identifications, not cipher-only proofs.

The conventional separator `X` additionally assumes baseline `Y→X`.
The `Y` in *bayr.* and *Livazeny* assumes baseline `7→Y`; the latter place
also requires a counted `C→Z` repair. A fourth lexical layer keeps the
unchanged `Q` in the `QUART` abbreviation as `Q`. None of these lexical or
separator assumptions is silently included in the historical numeric map.

The [source crop](../../experiments/operational_recovery/sources/childs_p230_A.png)
shows complete frames of 232 and 230 coordinates without erasures.
The baseline-label output is:

```text
45YUND2L2YDIVYUMKRONSTADTY0YBA7RYKAVYBRIGYUMFOGARASVERSAMMELTYYOKMYVERLEGTHEUPTQUARTYNACHMUEHLBACHYYOKMXANRZXXU26OP
```

The same-length proposed edition, still in baseline-label space, is:

<details>

**Edited output:**

```text
JJ8YIYDYNORDWESTLYHERMANNSTADTYX8YLDWYDIVYUMMUEHLBACHYJX4YDIVYIMRAUMEHATSZEGYLIVAZEN7YYDRITTENSYYGENKDOY82KRONSTADTY
```

Part 3 needs seven coordinate substitutions and part 4 one. The first
part's `IYD` and final `Y` become separators only under the separator
hypothesis. Baseline `0` in the brigade field becomes `7` only in the new
historical layer.
The exact unchanged `Q` occurs at plaintext position 80 of part 4, cell
`DF`, from source coordinates 10 and 96 (one-based); reading it as ordinary
`Q` is recorded as its own lexical assumption.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p230-a-source-and-credit"></a>

### Source and credit

Printed p230 / PDF page 233, heading **30 November 1918**:
`BSL v ZON (09.26 p.m., December 1st); 2200; 1st and 2d TL missing`.
The missing parts have not been reconstructed. The source is J. Rives
Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

Context comes from Franchet d'Esperey's 19 November 1918 telegram,
document 39, printed p79 / PDF page 153 in *Documents diplomatiques français
sur l'histoire du Bassin des Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I (Budapest, 1993).
The [provenance record](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
identifies the edition and scan. This telegram reports formations as of
11 November; it does not directly establish their locations at month end.

Published period-key attribution remains in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).
Source inspection, coordinate audit and this edition are by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python experiments/operational_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

The [input records](../../experiments/operational_recovery/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/certificates.json)
include literal rows, source hashes, individual edits, optional partial
squares, all domains and consistent re-encryption witnesses. Unassigned
cells in those witnesses are arbitrary consistency completions, not
accepted readings.

## Radio notices, Tiflis personnel and internment on p230

**Sources on this page:** p230 B, p230 C, p230 D, p230 E.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-radio-notices-tiflis-personnel-and-internment-on-p230"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four source-length telegrams on Childs p230 become complete literal readings under the published Nov28–Dec1 square. All 490 coordinates are preserved: no coordinate substitution, source-mask fill or frame change is needed. The source itself gives two first-group readings for C; both are retained.

<a id="source-p230-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-p230-b"></a>

### p230 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v CV (06.33 p.m., December 3d); 2130 (30/11); RICHI-136`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Inspektion und Kriegsministerium verstaendigt. Antwort steht noch aus. Papp.

**Meaning:** The inspection and the War Ministry have been notified; a reply is still outstanding. Signed Papp.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
INSPEKTIONUNDKRIEGSMINISTERIUMVERSTAENDIGTYYANTWORTSTEHTNOCHAUSYPAPP
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The page is headed 30 November; the intercept annotation says 3 December and the service line says 2130 (30/11). These are separate source dates.
- A small mark after the last V of VVGFV is not counted as a sixth coordinate. The source count is exactly 136.

<a id="source-p230-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-p230-c"></a>

### p230 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) CV v ZON (11.15 p.m., December 6th); 1900 (30/11); RIZI-78; XAFFV (or XVFFV)`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Station baut 0ZXJ frueh 9 Uhr ab. Burkard.

**Meaning:** A station announces when it will dismantle. The printed key labels do not establish the historical day or hour; Burkard is the literal signature.

The [shared late-November square](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
narrows the hour to **4 or 5**. Its `DX` pair is also the final digit of
`SCHWERE1?` on [p226 A2](226.md#edition-cases-radio-radio-traffic-transfer-fragment-a-date-and-station-field-that-must-be-read-together).
The earlier date-like field becomes `7Z12`, still garbled. Both printed
first-group variants remain in the
[additional-traffic certificate](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/traffic_certificate.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
STATIONBAUT0ZXJYFRUEH9YUHRABYYBURKARDYY
```

**Raw output — second printed source variant**, independently re-encrypted without repair.

```text
STATIONBAUT0ZXJZFRUEH9YUHRABYYBURKARDYY
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source explicitly prints XAFFV (or XVFFV). Both complete 78-slot frames are decrypted and re-encrypted. Their only output difference is position 15: Y versus Z. Neither version is silently selected as historically authentic.
- The readable text uses the first printed variant. Its literal field 0ZXJ and its hour label 9 stay unassigned. Under the alternative, the token immediately before FRUEH is 0ZXJZ rather than 0ZXJ followed by Y.
- The intercept annotation says 6 December; the service line says 1900 (30/11).

<a id="source-p230-d"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-p230-d"></a>

### p230 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) NKJ v LP (05.47 p.m., December 4th); Fuer COS 1225 (30/11); RICHI-188`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Zentralfunkleitg erbitten Nachricht ueber Verbleib Funker und Baupersonal der Funkenstation Tiflis. 54X05.

**Meaning:** The central radio command asks where the radio operators and construction personnel of the Tiflis station have gone. The final 54X05 remains a literal reference.

The closing reference reads **98179** under the
[shared late-November square](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md).
All five coordinate pairs are fully observed. The fourth digit uses the
newly supported `VG=7` assignment, at source positions 187 and 128; this
extends the earlier seven-record comparison by one numeral position.
No source repair is added. The number's documentary referent is unknown.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZENTRALFUNKLEITGERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERVERBLEIBFUNKERUNDBAUPERSONALDERFUNKENSTATIONTIFLISY54X05
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- ZENTRALFUNKLEITG is kept as the transmitted abbreviation; the readable display does not insert its omitted letters.
- The source header says 4 December; the service line says Fuer COS 1225 (30/11).

<a id="source-p230-e"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-p230-e"></a>

### p230 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) ZON v CV (04.43 p.m., December 6th); 0930 (30/11); RICHI-88`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Internierung rechtzeitig hierher mitteilen. Papp.

**Meaning:** Give timely notification here of the internment. Signed Papp. The short message does not name the persons or formation to be interned.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
INTERNIERUNGRECHTZEITIGHIERHERMITTEILENYPAPP
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The intercept annotation says 6 December; the service line reads 0930 (30/11). The earlier OCR gave 0830, which is not retained as the primary source transcription.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov30-radio-personnel-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.
